source: Aria Networks — Closing conversation: Deep Networking and token economics; Aria vs Arista's rise in the cloud era; NeoCloud and accelerator vendors
summary: AI cluster networking is the primary bottleneck and value driver for inference revenue, not just a cost-reduction tool
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI cluster networking is the primary bottleneck constraining inference revenue generation, not merely a cost-reduction lever, and that optimizing it can literally double utilization and therefore double revenue for AI factory operators. His reasoning draws a direct structural analogy to Arista's founding thesis — that Arista was built to solve the networking bottleneck that emerged as cloud hyperscalers scaled out — and applies the same logic to the inference era, where hundreds of billions of dollars of AI infrastructure sits underoptimized. The framing explicitly shifts from MFU (model flops utilization, a training-centric cost metric) to a revenue-generation lens: better networking means more tokens served per unit time, which means more inference revenue. Baker implies this represents a structural discontinuity that the market has not yet priced through first-principles thinking, making networking vendors purpose-built for AI inference clusters the primary investment beneficiary. The implication is that companies solving AI factory networking — analogous to what Arista did for cloud — are dramatically underappreciated as revenue enablers rather than cost-center vendors.

ticker_audit.reasoning: Baker explicitly draws the analogy between Arista's founding thesis (solving cloud-era networking bottlenecks) and the current AI inference networking opportunity. Arista is the canonical beneficiary of this structural framing and is directly named as the historical parallel, making it a direct beneficiary of the thesis even if the thesis is forward-looking toward newer entrants.

CoreWeave is a NeoCloud operator running large-scale AI inference infrastructure — exactly the type of operator Baker describes as sitting on hundreds of billions in underoptimized AI factory capacity. Better networking directly doubles their inference revenue, making them a direct beneficiary of the thesis being realized.
